title: Dead magic
summary: The lost magical arts of vanished or hidden cultures.

claims.text: Some mages hunt for the magic of ancient or secretive peoples, from early Africa and Mesopotamia to Greece, Rome and the Arctic.
Many of these arts were buried for good reason; some ask for sacrifices of virtue or of life, and few can practice them and stay sane.

title: The tale of Cagn
summary: A San story some Hermetics link to vampire legend.

claims.text: A San tale tells of Cagn, whose son was killed by baboons and whom Cagn brought back from death by magic.
Maya priests built a calendar so exact that it drifts only a day in about 6,000 years, since naming each moment correctly was central to their magic.
As they saw it, the world had already ended five times and been remade four, and the calendar was meant to pin down when the next ending would come.

title: The hungry sun
summary: The Aztec belief that sacrifice kept creation going.

claims.text: Aztec faith held that human blood and hearts fed the gods the strength to hold up creation, and that the sun needed blood to rise.
Mages who accept that shared belief shapes reality ask an uneasy question: whether, for that world, the sacrifices really were what held off its end.

title: The Oracle at Delphi
summary: The great oracle of ancient Greece.

claims.text: Greek kings, priests and common farmers alike traveled to Delphi before crowning a ruler, going to war or making any great choice.
Pilgrims paid the temple attendants, who examined the question; a young seer then breathed sulphurous fumes and spoke in a way only the attendants could read.

title: Innu hunting magic
summary: Old magic of the northern hunters.

claims.text: An Innu rite lets a child take the name of someone truly dead, along with a measure of that person's gifts; a ghost's name will not serve.
Hunters once shouted together as brant geese passed over, confusing the birds so they fell from the sky, and a good catch called for a great shared feast.
